## Direct-leader precheck owner evidence

The actual production-minted MCP call pauses at managed-worktree assessment.
Controlled ambiguous initial admission triggers actual construction abandonment,
closed publication, Git cleanup and construction release. Before correction, a
cold acquisition installed a second owner; the late accepted call changed disk
while the held/public note remained stale. The same regression now proves one
shared owner and zero cold reloads, equal disk/held/public notes, and cold history
again after all holds release. The hold begins before precheck and passes to
accepted cleanup, or releases on refusal/concurrent join; no TeamStore drain,
retirement, registry repair, second fence or broad admission counter changed.
Named tests are `holds the captured record through a direct leader precheck when
the initial submission fails and construction retires` and `releases refused
prechecks and concurrent join holds while one accepted dissolve owns cleanup` in
`packages/dreamux/tests/team-record-owner-lifetime.test.ts`. This uses real Team,
lease, filesystem and Git owners with controlled runtime IO, not a real-model
concurrency claim.

## R75 same-owner coverage and narrow supersession

The source deletes the ordered predictor, transient inode/name ledger, link expansion/case disambiguation and separate config-unlink/nonrecursive-root branch. Root uses the same existing owned-path remover as state/run/cache/log. Provider safety checks happen before service mutation; service removal then happens first among removal steps; pathExists guards each actual step, dry-run writes nothing, and actual rm recursively removes the root. The now-unused ENOTEMPTY predicate is deleted. Existing result types remain; no unknown status, warning fallback, permission oracle, cache or simulator was introduced.

| Prior acceptance row/family | Exact current title | Retained facts and R75 change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R453-UNINSTALL, foreign file/directory/none | previews without writes and recursively removes the root with %s foreign content | Preview preserves config, tree and foreign bytes and passes dryRun to service commands. Actual root is removed in all three cases; the former foreign-retained/skipped result is superseded. Equality is asserted only for these ordinary stable fixtures. |
| R453-UNINSTALL-LINK, four JSON/TOML dangling cases | recursively removes a dangling %s config link with the root (target removed first: %s) | Preview preserves actual links and target existence. Actual root deletion includes the dangling links. Their former persistence and retained root are superseded. |
| Ordered JSON/TOML config-unlink family, three cases | removes linked configs with the root without following external targets (JSON %s, TOML through JSON: %s) | Preview leaves both configs/links intact. Whole-root deletion removes both names while real external link target bytes remain. No config unlink sequencing or TOML-caused root retention is claimed. |
| R453-UNINSTALL-LINK-PARENT | removes root links without following a config target containing link-before-parent traversal | A currently readable linked config and its external target are real fixtures; preview preserves them and actual removal deletes root links but leaves target bytes. The removed predictor no longer owns raw-component link-before-parent resolution. |
| R453-UNINSTALL-DIRECTORY-ORDER, two cases | previews current run-link existence but actual removal observes state removed first (state is a link: %s) | Preview reports run removed because it currently resolves. Actual state removal makes run missing before its own step, and root is removed afterward. The test explicitly expects this one status difference. External state target bytes survive the state-as-link case. Exact predictive parity and retained root are superseded. |
| R453-UNINSTALL-ENTRY-IDENTITY | removes root hard links while preserving an external hard link | Actual same-inode names inside the root are deleted; the external link and its bytes remain. The old owned-versus-foreign entry-key predictor and foreign local-name retention are superseded. |
| R453-UNINSTALL-RELATIVE | previews without writes and recursively removes a relative DREAMUX_ROOT | Relative root addressing, all four owned dirs/config bytes and no-write preview remain. Actual root deletion includes former foreign content. |
| R453-UNINSTALL-UNIT-PERMISSION | removes a known systemd unit beneath a write-search-only parent and its dangling config link with the root | The actual unprivileged mode-0300 unit parent rejects readdir. Preview preserves bytes/modes; actual unit/root are removed; sibling unit outside Dreamux root remains. Former dangling config/root retention is superseded. |
| R453-UNINSTALL-ANCESTOR-PERMISSION | predicts full uninstall beneath a writable searchable ancestor without read permission | Existing fixture remains meaningful: actual mode-0333 ancestor denies readdir but known readable child root can be previewed and removed. Outside sibling and mode remain. Equality is for this fixture, not a general syscall-success promise. |
| R453-UNINSTALL-CASE, Config.json/State | previews actual filesystem lookup for %s and recursively removes both case variants | Setup observes actual case lookup, preview preserves contents, and actual recursive root deletion removes both variants. No special case-folding predictor or foreign capitalized-name retention remains. Only the local filesystem branch can be claimed by a gate run. |
| Missing root | dry-run and real uninstall report a missing root consistently | Preserved unchanged. Both report missing without requiring or creating the root. |

| R75-PROTECTED-PROVIDER-HOME | protects the provider-derived %s directory and its descendants before service removal | Actual custom CODEX_HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR roots and child paths reject in both modes before service calls; private protected marker bytes remain. R34 is preserved, not replaced by package-name checks. |
| R75-NESTED-PROVIDER-HOME | protects %s nested beneath a removal root before any service mutation | Actual CODEX_HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR marker bytes beneath root/state/run/cache/log survive both preview and real refusal. Service/config bytes survive and service-runner calls are empty. The existing pre-service predicate rejects containment in either direction. |
| R75-ROOT-LINK | uses access-based root-link existence without recursively following the link (dangling: %s) | Live root link is removed after ordinary owned-subdirectory steps; target config/foreign bytes remain. Already dangling root is missing under access and its link remains. Preview changes neither. These are next's actual access/rm semantics, not a new link policy. |
| R75-UNREADABLE-ROOT | previews an unreadable root without writes and propagates actual recursive removal EACCES (foreign content: %s) | Actual Linux uid1001 root mode0300, with/without foreign bytes: readdir fails, preview reports removal with no unknown warning, known bytes/modes unchanged; real recursive rm rejects EACCES. Finally restores permissions; fixtures are private. Both default and enabled full runs execute both cases. |


All rows above are actual private filesystem/owner evidence with fake service commands. Current permission evidence is Linux uid1001; case checks actually exercised the sensitive Config.json/State branch, not an insensitive volume. The previous nonrecursive-root ENOTDIR and config-unlink EISDIR/EPERM limitations describe deleted operations and are no longer current claims. Actual recursive filesystem errors still propagate; no mount detector or universal syscall-success prediction exists.

The six historical uninstall/service-only identities remain mapped to their same named owner assertions: four in uninstall.test and two in daemon.test. No entire historical case is retired by R75. The old ledger wording at deleted-tests.md:2123–2126 says owned config/state/logs were refused; the historical uninstall assertion documented in the deleted-tests ledger removes those paths. That body is the evidence. R75 supersedes only the former repair additions' foreign-content retention and future-step prediction assertions, as itemized above.

The round-nine corrections stay: Feishu's ordinary pending note accurately retains the creation-time message-id reminder; Team create/acceptedRequest/MCP descriptions no longer promise claims beyond a valid accepted record; only the newly restored README phrase/index/regex scan was removed. The same historical secure-default identity maps per fact to actual gate/schema/pairing/permissions/config/doctor owners, including missing-directory0700/first-file0600, literal persisted defaults, operator-policy and existing-trust preservation, retired diagnostics accepted then omitted, actual config path and unchanged doctor result with damaged configured Feishu access state. Unrelated pre-existing lexical cases are untouched. No count is claimed as coverage proof.

The two production `activity/reader.ts` edits (Codex and Claude) change comments only: native size bounds remain provider-owned; Core checks page/record shape, count and recognized errors, as the corrected `dreamux-types/src/agent-runtime.ts` comment states. No activity validation behavior was changed to satisfy an old test. Provider reader tests and the real growing-rollout case exercise the retained behavior.

`routing/index.ts` keeps its original fromRecord decoder private again. The two cross-module consumers were exact bindingFor lookups, so provisioning waiters and binding-card fallback now use their already-scoped input.target/target after the same ownership checks. Actual parent fallback still carries plan.matched from route planning. Visible/serving-target semantics, conversion behavior and the public package barrel remain unchanged; exact-target and parent/exact-topic assertions are recorded separately.

`TeamService.publishTeamState` additionally restores `if (!this.deps.coreEvents.hasSources()) return;` for the retained no-audience obligation (ledger 3720–3730 and R71 correction 5138–5143). It avoids aggregate/roster materialization and publication with no source. Committed roster observations continue; subscribing later replays nothing, and a later actual leader transition publishes the current roster. This is separate from deleting the frozen forwarding publisher object; the named owner test asserts all three observable phases. AgentServiceFactory.bind now uses the same existing hasSources capability only around teammate.state DTO publication; durable committed observers and roster recording continue before any audience exists. The new R453-IDENTITY-AUDIENCE case asserts those facts with actual owners. No new publisher, event queue or replay mechanism was introduced.

R54 supersedes only delegate-provided/frozen identity; tools still have describe-once, canonical-copy and freeze assertions. R48 supersedes only the removed created hook/scheduling/drain; the complete surviving real Server → Dispatcher launch → Team → leaderLaunch chain, frozen hook tables, durable workspace and consumed launch drafts are restored, with R52 names. These mixed obligations are recorded as mixed rows rather than retired wholesale.


The three fresh startup history scans retain the documented 3N disk-read cost. There is no cross-phase startup snapshot/history cache. TeamStore's captured-owner retain/release/drain and exact-map-identity check remain untouched. Existing R72/R73 and other settled deltas remain unchanged.


The ChannelProvider minimal fixture still compiles without optional capabilities and its createSession call returns the supplied instance; only its restoration-added self-enumeration was removed. The three historical boundary identities remain in the matrix. Transport's narrow removals are Stage2a item11's six names and Stage8b item1's internal narrowMetaFromEvent/FeishuMessageReader; the latter functions survive through public envelope decode and message reads. No unrelated barrel rewrite or blanket ABI retirement occurred.
